clue.text: Severe physician beginning to cut wine intake

parts.note: DR is the usual abbreviation for doctor, a physician
Asti is a sparkling Italian wine

indicators.note: beginning to a word means its first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A stern doctor tells a patient to start cutting down on drinking wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning to' gives C from 'cut', which goes inside ASTI by way of 'intake'.
explanation.definitionFit: Drastic measures are extreme or harsh ones, so severe is a synonym.

clue.text: Group who've retired turn up for discussions

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the whole run is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a set is a group of people or things
people who have retired for the night are abed

explanation.surface: A club of pensioners shows up for some talks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn up' reverses SETABED as one run; the surface's retirees are pensioners, but the cryptic sense is going to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Debates are formal arguments, a kind of discussion.

clue.text: Missile base having stiffening effect?

definitions.note: the definition describes a thing used to thicken, so it stands for a noun by example

parts.note: an arrow is a missile shot from a bow
a root is the base of something

explanation.surface: An arrow is fired at a base in the hope of making it rigid.
explanation.walkthrough: Arrowroot starch is used in cooking to thicken sauces; the question mark flags the loose definition by description.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrowroot is a starch that firms up liquids, so it has a thickening effect.

clue.text: Expert with pitch-fork?

parts.note: read the pitch-fork as a tuning fork: a person skilled at setting musical pitch, as for a piano

explanation.surface: A farmhand skilled with a pitchfork.
explanation.walkthrough: The pitchfork suggests hay, but a tuning fork gives musical pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A piano technician adjusts instruments to correct pitch, using a fork that rings a note.

clue.text: Docked, in isolation

definitions.meaning: docked means shortened or severed, as a tail
isolated, separated from contact with others

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from severing: a docked tail is severed, and an isolated village is severed from the world.

clue.text: Using gun pick off denizen of the wetlands

indicators.note: off means not right, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: With a rifle, someone shoots a creature living in the marshes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' signals an anagram of GUN and PICK; the denizen sounds like an animal but is a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The kingcup, or marsh marigold, is a yellow flower that grows in boggy ground.

clue.text: Go like clockwork

parts.note: to run as a well-regulated clock does, marking the beat accurately

explanation.surface: Things run smoothly.
explanation.definitionFit: A musician or a watch that holds a regular beat does just what a clock does.

clue.text: At ten, maybe, use phone for idle gossip

indicators.note: maybe signals the letters could be arranged differently

parts.note: to ring someone is to use the phone

explanation.surface: Someone calls at ten o'clock just to chat about nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges AT TEN into NATTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Nattering is a British word for chatting idly at length.

clue.text: Held on, though about to take a breather

parts.note: C is short for circa, about
a lung is an organ that breathes

explanation.surface: A climber holds on but must pause to take a breath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breather' suggests a rest, but here it is the organ we breathe with.
explanation.definitionFit: To cling is to hold on tight, and the past tense matches.

clue.text: He's throwing a pavingstone

definitions.meaning: the baseball player who throws the ball to the batter
a squared stone used for paving, also called a sett

explanation.definitionFit: The same word names the bowler figure in baseball and, in Britain, a stone slab used in paving.

clue.text: He's entitled to get right one in a club

indicators.note: in places the right and the one within the club

parts.note: a bat is a club used in games
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is allowed to join a club if he does it right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entitled' means bearing a title, not deserving.
explanation.definitionFit: A baronet holds a hereditary title, so he is entitled in the literal sense.

clue.text: Stunt about to go wrong? Rely on it!

indicators.note: letters that go wrong fall out of order and must be reshuffled

parts.note: RE is Latin for concerning, about

explanation.surface: A risky stunt is about to fail, you can be sure of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go wrong' rearranges STUNT with RE; the definition is an exclamation offering trust.
explanation.definitionFit: To commit something to someone's care is to rely on them to keep it.

clue.text: Powerful tug — to 'be re-lied upon

definitions.meaning: jokingly, a strong vessel that tows, a tower full of might
someone depended upon again and again for support

explanation.definitionFit: A person who gives unfailing support in trouble is a pillar others lean on.

clue.text: They guide water flow from boatload of fish

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'They guide water flow from boatload of fish (6)': the parse SS (boat) holding POUT (fish) makes the single word 'boatload' give the SS and also signal the containment, one word doing two jobs.
annotationWithheld.clue: They guide water flow from boatload of fish

clue.text: Heavy pressure of sole and burbot on cargo boat

indicators.note: on here means added on, so the fish follows the boat

parts.note: a tramp is a cargo ship with no fixed route
the burbot is a freshwater fish also called a ling

explanation.surface: A fish shop lists sole and burbot shipped on a cargo vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sole' looks like the fish beside the burbot, but it is the sole of a foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Trampling is crushing underfoot, heavy treading by the soles of feet.

clue.text: To make me resentful, bring me back a bird with the tail missing

indicators.note: bring back means the word me is turned round

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the last letter of the bird is removed

parts.note: the bittern is a marsh bird of the heron family

explanation.surface: Someone sulks that a bird was brought back to them without its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ME into EM; 'with the tail missing' removes N from BITTERN.
explanation.definitionFit: To sour someone or fill them with bitterness is to make them resentful.

clue.text: Has a meal among the crew-one reason for late arrival

indicators.note: among sets the dining inside the sailors

parts.note: tars are sailors, the crew of a ship
someone who dines has a meal

explanation.surface: A sailor stays to eat with his shipmates and so arrives late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the crew' are sailors, tars in crossword shorthand; the dash in the surface hides the switch to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being slow or behind time is lateness, which explains arriving late.

clue.text: Security device to prevent eight breaking in

indicators.note: breaking in puts the eight inside the other word

parts.note: to stop something is to prevent it
a rowing eight is a crew

explanation.surface: A lock designed to stop eight burglars breaking in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eight' is a rowing crew; the surface suggests burglars.
explanation.definitionFit: A threaded lid seals a jar or bottle securely.

clue.text: Charm one's way in

definitions.meaning: to charm is to enchant, delight utterly
a door or gate through which one enters

explanation.definitionFit: Stressed on the second syllable the word means to enchant; on the first, it is a doorway.

clue.text: Where the straying sheep lead us

indicators.note: lead puts the sheep first, ahead of us
straying sheep wander out of order, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: We follow lost sheep wherever they wander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'straying' rearranges SHEEP into EPHES, which leads US; the definition is just 'Where', a place.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephesus was an ancient Greek city in Asia Minor, a place.

clue.text: Fungus from a cigar that's gone off

indicators.note: a cigar that has gone off has gone bad, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Mould growing on a stale cigar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone off' suggests decay, matching the fungus, but signals rearranging A CIGAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Agaric is a mushroom with gills, such as the fly agaric.

clue.text: Makes boxes, boxing in everyone

indicators.note: boxing in places the letter inside the boxes

parts.note: crates are boxes
E stands for each, that is every one

explanation.surface: A factory makes boxes and packs everybody inside them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxing in' sets E inside CRATES.
explanation.definitionFit: To create is to make or bring into being.

clue.text: Foreign office furniture

definitions.meaning: the French word for an office

explanation.definitionFit: The French word for office is borrowed in English for a government department and a writing desk.

clue.text: Is expected to succeed

parts.note: read 'succeed' as inherit: one who stands next in line to a title unless someone closer is born

explanation.surface: Someone is tipped for success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'succeed' looks like doing well, but means coming after in a line of inheritance.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a person will inherit unless a nearer relative is born, so succession is expected, not certain.

clue.text: Girl with little house in America

definitions.note: the definition names a place located in America, standing for the place itself

parts.note: Ida is a girl's name
HO is the abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: A girl living in a small house in the States.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a place in America, a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is a state of the United States, located in the north-west.

clue.text: Whiting in oil not suitable for the meal

definitions.text: Whiting in oil not suitable for the meal

parts.words: Whiting in oil not suitable for the meal
parts.note: whiting here is powdered chalk, not the fish, and mixed with linseed oil it makes a glazing paste no one could eat

explanation.surface: A whiting cooked in oil turns out not fit to serve.
explanation.walkthrough: Whiting is ground chalk; the fish is a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: Glaziers' paste is chalk powder worked into linseed oil, plainly inedible.

clue.text: Attempts to withdraw silver filling in main setting

indicators.note: filling places the silver inside the other part
withdrawing means going back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: tries are attempts
AG is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Someone tries to take silver out of a mine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to withdraw' reads the attempts backwards before 'filling' adds the silver. The main is an old word for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Girt by sea means surrounded by ocean, set in the main as an island is.

clue.text: One must very much want to do it

definitions.text: One must very much want to do it

parts.words: One must very much want to do it
parts.note: describes pleading earnestly, which one does only when wanting something badly

explanation.surface: Only real desire makes someone do this.
explanation.definitionFit: To beg or plead earnestly shows strong desire for something.

clue.text: Close ranks as an emergency measure

definitions.meaning: read literally, to fill in a hole in a line
a temporary fix used until something better is found

explanation.definitionFit: Plugging a hole is a makeshift, temporary remedy.

clue.text: Old voyager employs sly outcast aboard

indicators.note: aboard puts the jumbled letters inside the other word

parts.note: to employ something is to use it

indicators.note: cast out here means thrown about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An ancient sailor takes on a shifty castaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outcast' scrambles the sly letters before 'aboard' puts them inside. Ulysses is the Latin name of Odysseus.
explanation.definitionFit: Odysseus, called Ulysses by the Romans, voyaged home from Troy for ten years.
